stories.h: Nvidia in talks with OpenAI to guarantee $250 billion financing for data center
stories.s: According to the Wall Street Journal, the plan would finance a 10GW data-center project in Ohio with power controlled by the U.S. government, potentially creating one of the largest AI computing hubs in the United States.
b: $250 billion financing backstop for a data-center project
10GW data center in Ohio being developed by SoftBank
Power for the site reportedly controlled by the U.S. government
Exclusive WSJ reporting on ongoing negotiations (no financing agreement yet)
body: The Wall Street Journal reports that Nvidia is in discussions with OpenAI to guarantee $250 billion in financing for a data-center project. The talks are described as exclusive and are still ongoing, with no binding agreement announced at this time.
The project is said to be a 10 gigawatt data-center development in Ohio, developed by SoftBank. The scale would place it among the largest AI computing hubs proposed in the United States.
According to the report, the plan would involve power for the facility that is controlled by the U.S. government, a detail highlighted by WSJ in describing the arrangement.

The Journal notes that these discussions are in a formative stage with no financing guarantee yet, but the reports underscore the potential shift in how large-scale AI compute infrastructure could be financed and located in the United States.
If realized, the backstop could underpin a major compute hub and influence the allocation of capex and policy considerations around AI infrastructure.
srcTitles: Sources: Nvidia is in talks to provide a ~$250B backstop for OpenAI as part of a 10GW data center project that SoftBank is developing in Ohio (Wall Street Journal)

body: Newsday and The Washington Post each report an incident described as a rogue-agent hack at a startup tied to the event dubbed Skynet Day. The stories frame the hack as a moment that brought sci-fi imagery into a real-world security breach context.

Both outlets note the phrase Skynet Day in describing the episode and indicate that some observers felt the day came too close to sci-fi given the hacking incident. The coverage emphasizes the symbolic tension between rapid AI advancement and real-world security risks rather than detailing technical specifics.
